title: Contents
markdown:
# Contents

Perron is the design system of Mylder, a live map of Copenhagen's public transport: every bus, S-tog, metro and regional train, where it is now, and how sure we are about that. The map is the product. Everything else floats over it on glass and says, in words and in the shape of every dot, how sure we are about what it shows.

## The brand

Mylder is Danish for a swarm or a throng: the city's vehicles, moving all at once. It has one look, in a light and a dark theme.

- **Honest.** Every vehicle shows how fresh its data is, and every sentence says no more than the data knows.
- **Calm.** The map and the vehicles carry the colour. The interface around them is ink, glass and neutral surfaces, with the brand yellow kept for the main action.
- **Of Copenhagen.** The operators' own line colours, the city's names, Danish and English side by side, the 24-hour clock.

The mark is on [Logos](logos.md), the brand colour on [Semantic colours](semantic-colours.md#brand), and the voice in [Content design](../content-design.md).

## Pages

Each page gives the rules for one foundation, then its tokens or files. The tables are rebuilt from the package's `tokens/`, `icons/` and `logos/` folders by `npm run tokens`, so a page always shows what the build ships. Edit the prose around a table, never the table.

| Page                                      | What it covers                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Accessibility](accessibility.md)         | The WCAG 2.2 AA target: what the build enforces, what a person checks |
| [Elevation](elevation.md)                 | The surface ladder, glass and shadows                                 |
| [Icons](icons.md)                         | The icon files, their size scale and style                            |
| [Layout](layout.md)                       | Breakpoints, the map screen, stacking and shared measures             |
| [Logos](logos.md)                         | The Mylder mark and how it is used                                    |
| [Motion](motion.md)                       | Durations, easing and reduced motion                                  |
| [Primitive colours](primitive-colours.md) | The palette every colour token points at                              |
| [Semantic colours](semantic-colours.md)   | Every colour token in both themes                                     |
| [Semantic spacing](semantic-spacing.md)   | Spacing, radius, border widths and the focus ring                     |
| [Typography](typography.md)               | The three families, the sixteen roles, sizes and line heights         |

Two more pages hold what only a live map needs:

| Page                          | What it covers                                       |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| [Data states](data-states.md) | The five Prik states, delays and kinds of disruption |
| [Map](map.md)                 | Line widths, dot sizes and dimming on the map canvas |

## Using the tokens

- Install `@mylder/perron` and load `@mylder/perron/perron.css` once at the app root. It brings the fonts, the custom properties for both themes and for reduced motion, the typography classes and a few page defaults.
- Pages name tokens the way the sources do, `color.text.primary`. In CSS that token is `var(--perron-color-text-primary)`: `--perron-`, then the name with dots as hyphens. Never copy a value.
- In script, `@mylder/perron/tokens.ts` has every value per theme, typed by name, and the reduced motion values under `modifiers`.
- Light is the default theme. Set `data-theme="dark"` on any element for dark; without it, the system's dark mode applies. Reduced motion follows the system setting on its own.
- Icons and logos are SVG files in `@mylder/perron/icons/` and `@mylder/perron/logos/`, listed with their use in `icons.json` and `logos.json`.
- A token changes only in Perron's own repository, in `packages/perron/tokens/*.tokens.json`, followed by `npm run tokens`. Never edit a generated file, or a table on these pages, by hand.

title: Accessibility
markdown:
# Accessibility

Perron targets [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) level AA. Part of it the build proves on every change: `npm run check` fails when any check below breaks. The rest no build can see, so a person checks it on every screen before it ships.

## What the build checks

- **Text contrast (1.4.3).** Every text colour reaches 4.5:1 on `color.surface.default`, `raised` and `inset`, in both themes. The test lists the deliberate misses by name: `color.text.tertiary` and `color.transit.delay.unknown`, which are only for hints, captions and the "—" of an unknown delay, always next to stronger text. Status and brand text also reach 4.5:1 on their own tinted surfaces.
- **Non-text contrast (1.4.11).** What shows where a control is, or what state something is in, reaches 3:1 against every surface: `color.border.control`, `color.border.brand`, the focus ring and the status fills. Decorative lines, `color.border.subtle` and `color.border.strong`, are exempt, and their descriptions say so.
- **The focus ring (2.4.7, 1.4.11)** reaches 3:1 on every surface and on the map's land, water and parks.
- **The surface ladder.** `color.surface.inset` stands apart from `color.surface.raised` by at least 1.15:1 in both themes, so an inset track reads without a border. See [Elevation](elevation.md#surfaces).
- **Line badges.** Label colours on line colours are measured, and the official pairs that miss are listed. See [Semantic colours](semantic-colours.md#line-colours).
- **Reduced motion (2.3.3, a AAA criterion met anyway)** lives in the tokens: when the system asks for less motion, transitions take 0.01 ms. See [Motion](motion.md).

### Text on surfaces

<!-- /contrast -->

## Rules

- **Focus.** Every interactive element shows the ring on `:focus-visible`: a `focus.width` solid outline in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` away from the element. `perron.css` sets it for the whole page. Never remove an outline without drawing the ring another way.
- **Targets (2.5.8).** Anything people press is at least `size.target-min` square, or has that much room around it. Perron's controls are larger: the smallest, a small button, is `size.button-sm`.
- **Colour never alone (1.4.1).** A status colour comes with a word or an icon, a data state with its name next to the dot, a line colour with the line's name.
- **Hover (1.4.13).** Anything shown on hover is also reachable by selecting the item, because touch and keyboard users never see hover. A hover card stays while the pointer is over it and closes with Esc.
- **Keys.** Esc closes the topmost thing first: a dialog, then a detail panel, then a highlight. + and − zoom, arrow keys pan.
- **State in words.** Toggles say their state in words as well as in looks ("Follow" / "Following"). One primary action per panel.
- **Moving things.** Loops (the follow blink and the report and selection pulses) stop in their component when the system asks for less motion. The tokens only shorten transitions.

<!-- tokens: focus.* size.target-min -->

| Token             | Value                    | Use                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `focus.width`     | `2px` (border.width.050) | Width of the focus ring                                               |
| `focus.offset`    | `2px`                    | Gap between the focused element and its ring                          |
| `size.target-min` | `24px`                   | Smallest touch or pointer target, from WCAG 2.2 target size (minimum) |

<!-- /tokens -->

## What a person checks

Before a screen ships, check what the build can't:

- **Keyboard.** Every action is reachable in a sensible order. Only an open dialog traps focus, and closing anything returns focus to where it came from.
- **Names.** Every control has an accessible name; an icon button carries a label. The map has a text alternative: the vehicle list.
- **Images.** Images and the mark have alt text, or are hidden from assistive technology when they are decoration.
- **Zoom and reflow (1.4.4, 1.4.10).** At 200% zoom and at 320 px wide, nothing is cut off or overlaps, and only the map scrolls sideways.
- **Text spacing (1.4.12).** Wider line, letter and word spacing breaks nothing.
- **Announcements.** Live updates, such as countdowns and moving vehicles, don't flood a screen reader: a polite live region announces changes of state only.
- **Forced colours.** In Windows' contrast themes, the focus ring and the selected state still show. The Prik shapes keep each data state readable without colour.

title: Elevation
markdown:
# Elevation

The surface and shadow tokens. The map is the ground; everything else floats over it, and depth shows first in the surface colour, then in a shadow.

## Surfaces

- Floating panels are glass: `color.surface.overlay` with a backdrop blur of `effect.glass-blur` and a saturation of `effect.glass-saturate`. On phones, panels full of text use `color.surface.default` instead, so text never sits on moving map.
- Inside a panel, cards and inputs sit on `color.surface.raised`, and tracks, counts and inset boxes on `color.surface.inset`.
- Hover is `color.surface.hover`, laid over whatever is beneath. A selected row is `color.surface.selected`.
- `color.surface.inverse` is the primary button, pressed toggles and the chart's value tip, with `color.text.inverse` on it.

<!-- tokens: color.surface.default color.surface.raised color.surface.inset color.surface.overlay color.surface.hover color.surface.selected color.surface.inverse effect.* -->

| Token                    | Light                           | Dark                            | Use                                                                |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `color.surface.default`  | `#FAFBF9` (palette.neutral.50)  | `#12181B` (palette.neutral.900) | Opaque panel background; text on inverse surfaces                  |
| `color.surface.raised`   | `#FFFFFF` (palette.neutral.0)   | `#1D2428` (palette.neutral.800) | Inputs, selected segment                                           |
| `color.surface.inset`    | `#EBEEEB` (palette.neutral.100) | `#283237` (palette.neutral.700) | Segmented control track, counts, inset boxes                       |
| `color.surface.overlay`  | `rgba(250, 251, 249, 0.9)`      | `rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.88)`        | Translucent floating panels over the map (used with backdrop blur) |
| `color.surface.hover`    | `rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.05)`        | `rgba(235, 238, 235, 0.06)`     | Hover state layer                                                  |
| `color.surface.selected` | `rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.09)`        | `rgba(235, 238, 235, 0.09)`     | Selected row                                                       |
| `color.surface.inverse`  | `#12181B` (color.text.primary)  | `#EBEEEB` (color.text.primary)  | Primary buttons, pressed icon buttons, chart tooltip               |
| `effect.glass-blur`      | `16px`                          | `16px`                          | Backdrop blur behind glass panels                                  |
| `effect.glass-saturate`  | `1.3`                           | `1.3`                           | Backdrop saturation behind glass panels                            |

<!-- /tokens -->

Inset stands apart from raised in both themes, so a track reads without a border: a step darker in light, a step lighter in dark. The build keeps the two at least 1.15:1 apart.

<!-- contrast 1.15: color.surface.inset on color.surface.raised -->

| Colour                | Light raised | Dark raised |
| --------------------- | ------------ | ----------- |
| `color.surface.inset` | 1.17:1       | 1.20:1      |

<!-- /contrast -->

## Shadows

Floating panels carry `shadow.panel`. Nothing else casts a shadow, except the selected segment of a segmented control, with `shadow.thumb`. Both are set per theme: a dark surface needs a darker, wider shadow to show at all.

<!-- tokens: shadow.* -->

| Token          | Light                                                                             | Dark                                                                         | Use                                     |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `shadow.panel` | `0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.06), 0px 10px 30px 0px rgba(18, 24, 27, 0.1)` | `0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35), 0px 14px 36px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.38)` | Floating panels                         |
| `shadow.thumb` | `0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.14)`                                             | `0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)`                                         | Selected segment in a segmented control |

<!-- /tokens -->

Stacking order is on [Layout](layout.md#stacking).

title: Icons
markdown: # Icons One small set, drawn for Mylder. Perron draws its own stroke icons rather than use an icon font or a third-party set: there are few of them, each drawn on a grid near the size it shows at. The files are in `packages/perron/icons/`, and `icons.json` there lists them by category with the size and use of each. ## Sizes Every icon renders at one of three steps, set with `--perron-icon-size` (one of the tokens below) and never with a raw width. Each icon is drawn on the grid closest to its step, so its stroke stays between 1.5 and 1.8 px. A larger icon is a new drawing, not a scaled one. | Token | Value | Use | | --------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | | `icon.size.325` | `13px` | Inline with label and caption text: the disruption icons | | `icon.size.400` | `16px` | Inside controls: search, zoom, locate, close | | `icon.size.450` | `18px` | Top bar buttons: kiosk mode, about | ## Style - Strokes with round caps and joins, 1.5 to 1.8 px on the icon's own grid. Fills only for a dot, such as the point of the info icon. - Drawn in `currentColor`, so an icon takes the colour of the text around it. Set the colour on the text, never on the icon. - The `.perron-icon` class in `perron.css` sizes an inline SVG icon from `--perron-icon-size`, and keeps it from shrinking in a flex row. - An icon sits next to a word or inside a labelled button; it never carries meaning alone. Next to text it is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden="true"`). Alone, it needs an accessible name. - No icon font, no emoji, no third-party icon set. A new icon follows this page, joins `icons.json`, and the check confirms its grid, stroke and colour. ## The set ### Map | Icon | Name | Grid | Size | Use | | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------- | | | `plus` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | Zoom in | | | `minus` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | Zoom out | | | `locate` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | Centre the map on the network | ### Actions | Icon | Name | Grid | Size | Use | | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- | | | `search` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | The search field | | | `close` | 16 px | `icon.size.400`, 16 px | Close a panel, a dialog or a highlight | ### App | Icon | Name | Grid | Size | Use | | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----- | ---------------------- | -------------- | | | `monitor` | 18 px | `icon.size.450`, 18 px | Kiosk mode | | | `info` | 18 px | `icon.size.450`, 18 px | About and help | ### Disruptions | Icon | Name | Grid | Size | Use | | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----- | ---------------------- | ------------------ | | | `warning` | 14 px | `icon.size.325`, 13 px | Delays | | | `signal-off` | 14 px | `icon.size.325`, 13 px | Data feed problems | | | `diversion` | 14 px | `icon.size.325`, 13 px | Diversions | | | `calendar` | 14 px | `icon.size.325`, 13 px | Planned works |

title: Layout
markdown:
# Layout

Where the layout switches, and what the map screen is built from.

## Breakpoints

Each breakpoint is the width below which the screen changes.

- Under `breakpoint.desktop`, the filters that are coming later go.
- Under `breakpoint.tablet`, the city name, the date and the legend go.
- Under `breakpoint.phone`, the sheet and the detail panel become bottom sheets, and the top bar shrinks to `size.top-bar-phone`.
- Under `breakpoint.compact-phone`, the brand mark goes.

<!-- tokens: breakpoint.* -->

| Token                      | Value    | Use                            |
| -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------ |
| `breakpoint.compact-phone` | `380px`  | Hide the brand mark            |
| `breakpoint.phone`         | `760px`  | Bottom sheets, compact top bar |
| `breakpoint.tablet`        | `1180px` | Hide city name, day and legend |
| `breakpoint.desktop`       | `1400px` | Hide "Later" chips             |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Page shell

The map fills the screen, and the page shell floats over it.

- A top bar of glass groups runs along the top: brand, clock, filters and settings.
- The overview sheet sits on the left and the detail panel on the right.
- Map controls and the scale sit at the bottom right, and the legend at the bottom centre.
- Panels keep `size.panel-gap` from the screen edge and from each other.

<!-- tokens: size.top-bar size.top-bar-phone size.sheet-width size.detail-width size.sheet-peek size.panel-gap -->

| Token                | Value   | Use                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size.top-bar`       | `46px`  | Top bar group height (42 on phones)                                  |
| `size.top-bar-phone` | `42px`  | Height of a top bar group on phones                                  |
| `size.sheet-width`   | `376px` | Overview sheet width on desktop                                      |
| `size.detail-width`  | `364px` | Detail panel width on desktop                                        |
| `size.sheet-peek`    | `182px` | Bottom sheet height when closed on phones                            |
| `size.panel-gap`     | `12px`  | Distance between floating panels and the viewport edge (8 on phones) |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Stacking

From lowest to highest: map controls, the overview sheet, the highlight chip, the detail panel, the top bar, the tooltip, then a dialog over a `color.scrim` backdrop.

<!-- tokens: z-index.* color.scrim -->

| Token                  | Value                    | Use                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `z-index.map-controls` | `3`                      | Legend, map controls, scale, attribution          |
| `z-index.sheet`        | `4`                      | Overview sheet, kiosk bar                         |
| `z-index.highlight`    | `5`                      | Highlight chip                                    |
| `z-index.detail`       | `6`                      | Detail panel                                      |
| `z-index.top-bar`      | `7`                      | Brand, filters and clock along the top of the map |
| `z-index.tooltip`      | `8`                      | Map hover card, above every panel                 |
| `z-index.dialog`       | `10`                     | Modal dialog over everything                      |
| `color.scrim`          | `rgba(10, 14, 16, 0.42)` | Backdrop behind modal dialogs                     |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Other layout properties

A measure lives here when two places must agree on it, such as a component and the list that virtualises its rows. A measure only one component's CSS reads stays in that CSS.

<!-- tokens: size.control size.button size.button-sm size.input size.segment size.badge size.badge-lg size.vehicle-row size.target-min -->

title: Logos
markdown: # Logos The Mylder mark, and how it is used. The files are in `packages/perron/logos/`, and `logos.json` there lists them with the ground each is drawn for. ## The mark The mark is a bus dot, an S-tog dot and an estimated ring: three of the ways a vehicle can look on the map. Its colours are tokens, each in its theme's value: the bus dot is `color.transit.mode.bus`, the S-tog dot line A's `color.transit.line.a`, the ring `color.text.primary`. A file is an image and can't follow the theme, so there is one file per theme, and the check holds each file's colours to its theme's tokens. | Token | Light | Dark | Use | | ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | `color.transit.mode.bus` | `#D99A00` (palette.yellow.500) | `#F2B630` (palette.yellow.300) | All bus lines | | `color.transit.line.a` | `#00A1DE` | `#00A1DE` | S-tog A | | `color.text.primary` | `#12181B` (palette.neutral.900) | `#EBEEEB` (palette.neutral.100) | Main text and icons; also the focus ring | ## Usage - Keep the mark as drawn: its three shapes and colours are data states, so a recoloured, outlined or rearranged mark says something else. - Set it beside the wordmark: "mylder" in lowercase, in `typography.heading-md` set bold. The mark alone stands in only where space is tight, such as an app icon. - Keep clear space of at least the ring's width around it, and set it no smaller than its drawn size, 27 × 19 px. - Use the file drawn for the ground it sits on: `mylder-mark.svg` on light, `mylder-mark-dark.svg` on dark. ## Files ### Brand | Logo | File | Theme | Use | | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----- | ---------------- | | | `logos/mylder-mark.svg` | Light | On light grounds | | | `logos/mylder-mark-dark.svg` | Dark | On dark grounds |

title: Motion
markdown:
# Motion

Motion explains a change of place. The sheet slides, the camera eases to a selection, and meters ease to new values. Vehicles glide between reports instead of jumping.

## Durations

- **Transitions** move something from one place or value to another, once: `duration.sheet`, `duration.meter`, `duration.camera` and `duration.follow`.
- **Loops** repeat while something is true. A new report pulses once around its vehicle (`duration.report-pulse`), a ring pulses around the selected vehicle (`duration.selection-pulse`), and the follow indicator blinks while the camera follows (`duration.blink`).

<!-- tokens: duration.* -->

| Token                      | Value    | Reduced motion | Use                                                   |
| -------------------------- | -------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `duration.sheet`           | `320ms`  | `0.01ms`       | Bottom sheet open and close                           |
| `duration.meter`           | `800ms`  | `0.01ms`       | Meter fill change                                     |
| `duration.camera`          | `750ms`  | `0.01ms`       | Map camera fly-to                                     |
| `duration.follow`          | `500ms`  | `0.01ms`       | Camera fly-to when following starts                   |

| `duration.report-pulse`    | `1100ms` |                | Ring that expands when a vehicle reports its position |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Easing

The sheet has its own curve, which settles slowly so a long slide doesn't stop abruptly. Everything else eases with `easing.standard`, the browser's `ease`.

<!-- tokens: easing.* -->

| Token             | Value                              | Use               |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `easing.sheet`    | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)`   | Bottom sheet      |
| `easing.standard` | `cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)` | CSS ease (meters) |

<!-- /tokens -->

## Reduced motion

When the system asks for less motion, the transition tokens take 0.01 ms: their values under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` are in the table's Reduced motion column. The value is 0.01 ms rather than 0, so `transitionend` and animation events still fire. CSS that reads the tokens needs nothing more.

- **Loops** keep their durations in the tokens, because a loop at 0.01 ms would flicker. Each component that runs a loop stops it under reduced motion.
- Vehicles move to each new report without gliding.

The values come from the resolver's `motion` modifier. Its default context, `full`, is empty, because base already holds the full-motion values; its `reduced` context points at `packages/perron/tokens/motion-reduced.tokens.json`. The build writes the overrides into each output:

| Output               | Reduced motion                                                             |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tokens.css`         | The overrides inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, on `:root` |
| `tokens.ts`          | `modifiers.motion.reduced`, as CSS text and as numbers                     |
| `penpot.tokens.json` | A `motion-reduced` set, and a Motion group with Full and Reduced themes    |

## Timings in script

Script that animates, such as the map camera's fly-to, reads `numeric` from `tokens.ts`, and `modifiers.motion.reduced.numeric` when `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` matches. Both hold durations in milliseconds.

# Primitive colours

The palette holds Perron's raw colour values. Every `color` token points at a palette step in each theme, so retuning a step moves every colour built on it. Components and apps never read the palette: they use the `color` tokens on [Semantic colours](semantic-colours.md), and a new need gets a new `color` token, never a palette value.

## Steps

A neutral ramp runs from `0` (white) to `950`. Five hues, blue, green, orange, red and yellow, have five steps each. Steps rise as the colour darkens, and each hue step has one job:

- **100**: light-theme tint.
- **300**: dark-theme fill and text.
- **500**: light-theme fill.
- **700**: light-theme text, 4.5:1 on every light surface.
- **900**: dark-theme tint.

Gaps in the neutral ramp are room for new steps. A translucent colour is written in full on its `color` token, with a palette step's components plus an alpha, and a test checks its RGB is a palette step.

# Semantic colours

Every colour token in both themes. A `color` token says what a colour is for and points at a [primitive colour](primitive-colours.md) in each theme.

## Light and dark

- Light is the default theme. Dark comes from `data-theme="dark"` on any element or, without an explicit theme, from the system's dark mode. `data-theme="light"` keeps an element light inside a dark page, so one page can show both themes side by side.
- Both themes define the same names, and the build fails when one is missing.
- Dark colours are their own palette steps, chosen for the dark surfaces, not an inversion of the light ones: 300 for status and brand fills and text, 900 for tints, the light neutrals for text.
- Base tokens never point at a theme token. A custom property resolves where it is declared, so a base token built from a theme colour would keep the root theme's value inside a nested `data-theme`.

## Text

- Three text colours for the interface. Use `color.text.primary` for what people read first, and `color.text.secondary` for supporting text. Keep `color.text.tertiary` for hints, axis labels and captions next to stronger text: it misses 4.5:1 on purpose (the figures are on [Accessibility](accessibility.md)), so set sentences people must read in primary or secondary.
- `color.text.inverse` sits on `color.surface.inverse`, the primary button and pressed toggles.
- On a coloured fill, text is `color.text.on-color.dark` or `color.text.on-color.light`, whichever the fill was paired with.

# Semantic spacing

The spacing, radius and border tokens.

## Space

Every padding, margin and gap comes from the spacing scale: nine steps from 2 to 32 px on a 4 px base. The number divided by 100 is the count of 4 px units, so `space.300` is 12 px.

- Parts of a detail panel sit 12 px apart (`space.300`), and blocks of a pane 24 px apart (`space.600`).
- Panels sit 12 px from the screen edge and from each other (`size.panel-gap`, on [Layout](layout.md)).

| Token       | Value  |
| ----------- | ------ |
| `space.050` | `2px`  |
| `space.100` | `4px`  |
| `space.150` | `6px`  |
| `space.200` | `8px`  |
| `space.300` | `12px` |
| `space.400` | `16px` |
| `space.500` | `20px` |
| `space.600` | `24px` |

## Radius

Radius grows with the size of the thing it rounds.

<!-- tokens: radius.* -->

| `radius.xs`   | `4px`    | Small marks and ticks                   |
| `radius.sm`   | `6px`    | Line badges                             |
| `radius.md`   | `8px`    | Buttons, inputs, icon buttons, segments |

| `radius.xl`   | `16px`   | Floating panels, sheets and dialogs     |

## Border widths

Two widths, numbered like the spacing scale: `border.width.025` is a quarter of 4 px, `border.width.050` half. Hairlines and the edges of inputs, cards and panels take the thin one. The focus ring and the selected state of a control take the thick one.

<!-- tokens: border.width.* -->

## Focus ring

The ring is a solid outline, `focus.width` wide and `focus.offset` from the element, in `color.border.focus`. `perron.css` draws it on `:focus-visible` for every element; a component that draws its own ring uses the same three tokens.

markdown:
# Typography

Three families, self-hosted. Familjen Grotesk is for headings and the wordmark, Schibsted Grotesk for text and labels, and JetBrains Mono for data. Fonts load from this package, never from Google Fonts, which would send visitors' IP addresses to Google.

## Roles

Sixteen roles, one per job. Set every piece of text with a role, either as a class (`perron-typography-body`) or as a composite custom property (`font: var(--perron-typography-body)` plus `letter-spacing: var(--perron-typography-body-tracking)`).

- Anything people compare down a column is a `data` role: times, countdowns, counts, delays, percentages. They use tabular figures, so columns line up.
- `overline` sets its text in capitals: the class adds `text-transform: uppercase`, and with the custom property you add it yourself. Write the source text in sentence case.
- On phones, `display` and `data-xl` step down to `font.size.800`, and `stat` to `font.size.600`. These are the only places a component reaches for a size directly.

# Data states

Every vehicle is a Prik, drawn in its line colour in one of five states. The shapes are the system's signature: never reuse a ring or a dashed ring to mean anything else, and never draw a vehicle without its state.

| State          | Shape         | Means                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Live           | A solid dot   | A GPS report under a minute old                        |
| Ageing         | A fainter dot | A report 1 to 5 minutes old                            |
| Estimated      | A ring        | Placed from the timetable and the latest delay         |
| Timetable only | A dashed ring | No real-time data at all                               |
| No signal      | A grey dot    | Silent for over 5 minutes, left where it was last seen |

- Always write the state in words next to the dot. Legends list all five states, in this order, even when one has no vehicles.
- `color.data-state.no-signal` means a vehicle has gone silent. Use it for that alone.
- On the map, draw dots on a canvas, with a halo of `color.data-state.halo` and, for light line colours on the light map, a hairline of `color.data-state.outline`.

title: Content design
markdown:
# Content design

How every word in Mylder reads: plain sentences, exact about certainty, in English, Danish, Swedish and Norwegian Bokmål. The foundations are in [foundations/](foundations/README.md).

- Say what is happening in plain sentences, then how sure we are. "Signal fault at Danshøj. Trains between Flintholm and Ny Ellebjerg run slower than planned." Never claim more certainty than the data has: a vehicle without a signal is "No signal since 08:02", not a guess.
- Sentence case everywhere: "Show whole line", "Back to the map", "Reporting live, by operator". Capitals come only from the `perron-typography-overline` style, so write the source text in sentence case.
- Speak about the city and its vehicles, not about the person. Address them only in instructions: "Try a line number such as 5C."
- Numbers: 24-hour clock ("08:14"), a space before units ("4 min", "45 km/h"), the true minus sign for early ("−1"), "—" for unknown, "≈" before estimates, "~" before estimated times. Countdowns under 45 seconds read "Now".
- Data states and delays always use the words in the table below, in every language, so every screen agrees.
- Name keys in help text: "Keys: + and − zoom, arrows pan, Esc closes panels."
- No emoji, no exclamation marks.

## Data-state and delay words

Components take these from the locale dictionaries in `packages/perron/src/locale/`, which a test holds to this table. Change a word in this table and in the locale dictionaries together.

| English          | Danish        | Swedish          | Norwegian Bokmål |

| Live             | Live          | Live             | Live             |
| Ageing           | Ældre         | Äldre            | Eldre            |
| Estimated        | Beregnet      | Beräknad         | Beregnet         |
| Timetable only   | Kun køreplan  | Endast tidtabell | Kun rutetabell   |
| No signal        | Intet signal  | Ingen signal     | Ingen signal     |
| Delays           | Forsinkelser  | Förseningar      | Forsinkelser     |

title: Glossary
markdown:
# Glossary

The words used to talk about Perron, Mylder's design system. The words Mylder shows its riders are in [content-design.md](content-design.md).

## Layers

**Component**:
A reusable piece of interface built on Base UI, with MUI-shaped props and no knowledge of transit.
_Avoid_: Widget, primitive

**Pattern**:
A piece of a Mylder screen built only from components, which takes Mylder's domain data as props, such as a departure row.
_Avoid_: Composition, template, organism

## Building a component

**Contract**:
The rules every component follows: its props, events, styling, files and checks.
_Avoid_: Guidelines, conventions

**Spec**:
What a piece of work must do, written before it is built. A component's spec is its page in `docs/components/`: its anatomy, Base UI parts, props, tokens, keyboard behaviour and owned strings. Any other spec, such as one for a roadmap phase, is a GitHub issue.
_Avoid_: Brief, design doc

**Ticket**:
One sub-issue of a spec's issue: a slice of the work that can be built and checked on its own, naming the tickets that block it.
_Avoid_: Task, story

**Read-back**:
The machine-readable copy of a component's Penpot design, `penpot/<name>.json`, that code and checks are compared against.
_Avoid_: Export, snapshot

**Code map**:
The file that pairs each Penpot variant property and layer of a component with a React prop or CSS state.
_Avoid_: Mapping, Code Connect

**Gate**:
A point a component may not pass until a check or a person says yes.
_Avoid_: Step, checkpoint

**Pre-flight**:
The files a skill must read before it may write anything.
_Avoid_: Setup, context

**Owned string**:
A word a component shows or announces on its own, rather than one the caller passes, such as "Close". It comes from the locale dictionaries.
_Avoid_: Internal label, default text

**Intent**:
A value of a component's `color` prop, backed by tokens: what the colour means, not which colour it is.
_Avoid_: Tone, colour name

## The factory

**Factory**:
The local system of Claude Code runs that moves each component through the loop, from its issue to a ready PR.
_Avoid_: Pipeline, bot

**Run**:
One start of the factory on one component, from the moment it claims the issue to the next gate, cap or ready PR. It remembers only what the issue, the PR and `pipeline.yaml` hold.
_Avoid_: Session, job

**Scorecard**:
What one stage run records about itself in `pipeline.yaml`: its attempts, the checks that failed, its pre-flight reads, its review findings, its questions and its cost.
_Avoid_: Metrics, report

**Scorer**:
A rubric that a fresh-context agent applies to the transcripts of runs, giving each a pass, a fail or insufficient evidence, with a reason.
_Avoid_: Judge, eval, grader

**Touch**:
Anything the maintainer does for a component beyond the two gates: answering a `[PENDING]` question, clearing `needs-human`, sending a design back, asking for changes on the PR or pushing a commit to it.
_Avoid_: Steer, intervention

**Retro**:
The run that improves the factory itself. After every fifth merged component, it scores those runs and opens one PR to the instructions behind their failures.
_Avoid_: Self-improvement agent, outer loop

**Replay**:
One stage run again on a merged component's frozen inputs, to compare a proposed change with what it replaces.
_Avoid_: Shadow run, benchmark

title: Contract
markdown:
# Contract

The rules every Perron component follows: its files, props, events, styling, words, stories and checks. Components are built on Base UI (`@base-ui/react`), take props shaped like MUI's, and are styled in plain CSS with Perron's tokens. The reasons are in `docs/adr/0001-base-ui-with-mui-shaped-apis.md`, `docs/adr/0006-component-strings-from-locale-dictionaries.md` and `docs/adr/0007-patterns-layer.md`.

Every component starts as a spec, `docs/components/<name>.md`, and every pattern as one in `docs/patterns/<name>.md`, copied from the [Spec template](TEMPLATE.md). Read the [brand](../foundations/README.md) and [content design](../content-design.md) before writing one.

The rules the [Checks](#checks) table names fail `npm run check` when broken. The rest are held by the build's self-gate (the `component-build` skill's own pass over the stories, looped until clean before review) and by the reviewer.

## Files

`<Name>` is the component's name in PascalCase, `<name>` the same in kebab-case.

| File                                                       | Holds                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/perron/src/components/<Name>/<Name>.tsx`         | The component, and its props type `<Name>Props`, both exported                                                               |
| `packages/perron/src/components/<Name>/<Name>.css`         | Its styles, which the TSX imports: `import './<Name>.css'`                                                                   |
| `packages/perron/src/components/<Name>/<Name>.stories.tsx` | Its stories and `play` tests                                                                                                 |
| `packages/perron/src/components/<Name>/<Name>.mdx`         | Its Storybook docs page, written by the `component-docs` skill after review                                                  |
| `docs/components/<name>.md`                                | Its spec; a pattern's is `docs/patterns/<name>.md`                                                                           |
| `storybook/pages/<name>.mdx`                               | Its spec's Storybook page: `storybook/pages/contract.mdx` with the spec's path, titled `Specs/<Name>`                        |
| `components/<name>/`                                       | Its place in the loop: `pipeline.yaml`, which `npm run factory` alone writes, `review.md` and the visual report in `visual/` |

- One component per folder. A child the caller writes many times, such as a menu's item, is a component of its own, in its own folder.
- A component joins `packages/perron/components.json`, and `npm run registry` writes the barrel and the package exports from it.
- A component composes shared parts from `packages/perron/src/parts/<Part>/<Part>.tsx`, and other components from their own folders.

An entry's `status` in `packages/perron/components.json` says how far it has come, and what it has by then:

| Status       | Set when                                          | It has                                                                        |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `designing`  | It joins the registry                             | Nothing yet: it is not exported, listed or checked                            |
| `building`   | The build stage starts                            | Its code and its spec; it joins the barrels and the sidebar                   |
| `stable`     | Its docs stage is done, in the component's own PR | Its `<Name>.mdx` too, and a props API that only grows (see [Change](#change)) |
| `deprecated` | Its replacement is `stable`                       | Everything a stable entry has; it keeps working                               |

## Props

Base UI underneath, MUI's shape on top. Base UI comes from its public entry points, `@base-ui/react/<component>`; lint stops `@mui/*`, `@base-ui-components/*` and `@base-ui/react/internals/*`.

These names mean one thing in every component. A prop outside the list is the component's own: its spec names it, and the reviewer holds it to its siblings.

| Prop                                       | Type                                         | Rule                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`                                  | A union of string literals                   | The Penpot `variant` property, its values spelled as Penpot spells them. The default is the first.                   |
| `color`                                    | A subset of the [intents](#intents)          | Default `'neutral'`.                                                                                                 |
| `size`                                     | A subset of `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | Default `'medium'`.                                                                                                  |
| `disabled`, `fullWidth`, other booleans    | `boolean`                                    | An adjective, default `false`: `disabled`, `fullWidth`, `required`, `readOnly`. No `is`, `has` or `should` in front. |
| `startIcon`, `endIcon`                     | `ReactNode`                                  | An icon before or after the label, in reading order, so they swap sides in right-to-left text.                       |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`        | See [State and events](#state-and-events)    |                                                                                                                      |
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen`, `onClose` | See [State and events](#state-and-events)    |                                                                                                                      |
| `name`                                     | `string`                                     | On every control whose value a form submits.                                                                         |
| `render`                                   | Base UI's `render`                           | Swaps the root element. See [Customising](#customising).                                                             |
| `slotProps`                                | One key per inner Base UI part               | The only way inside. See [Customising](#customising).                                                                |
| `<key>Label`                               | `string`                                     | Overrides one owned string on one instance: `closeLabel`, `previousPageLabel`. See [Words](#words).                  |
| `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref`    | React's                                      | Reach the root. See [Root](#root).                                                                                   |

Every member the props type declares itself has a JSDoc comment. Members it inherits from Base UI or the HTML element keep theirs. The docs page's props table lists every member the props type declares and every one it inherits from Base UI, with Base UI's JSDoc and `@default`; the HTML element's attributes reach the root and get no row, as in MUI's tables. Its Default column shows each prop's destructuring default, or, where the component has none to write, the member's `@default`: a `render` the component declares itself says `@default <span />` with its own element, and an owned-string prop says `@default The locale's`, as the spec's Props table gives it.

The spec's Props table has the docs page's rows: one per member the props type declares, and one per member it inherits from Base UI, such as `render`. An inherited row reads `inherited` in its Base UI prop column and gives Base UI's type, `@default` and description. The row documents the member and asks nothing of the code: the props type inherits it and declares only its own members, so Base UI's JSDoc reaches the docs page unchanged. The `docs` check holds the two tables to each other (see [Checks](#checks)).

### Names from other libraries

Where another library takes a prop on the right, a Perron component takes what is on the left:

| Use                                                            | In place of               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `className`, the data attributes and the tokens                | `sx`, `classes`, `styled` |
| `render`                                                       | `component`, `as`         |
| The tokens, which carry both themes                            | `theme`                   |
| CSS states: pseudo-classes and Base UI's data attributes       | `state`                   |
| `onChange(event, value, details)`                              | `onValueChange`           |
| `onOpen(event, details)` and `onClose(event, reason, details)` | `onOpenChange`            |
| `startIcon`                                                    | `leftIcon`                |
| `endIcon`                                                      | `rightIcon`               |

### Intents

A `color` value is an intent: what the colour means. Each has its tokens; a component offers only the intents its spec gives tokens for. A new intent starts as tokens, through the `design-tokens` skill.

| Intent    | Text                 | Tinted surface               | Mark (icons, dots, meters) | Solid fill, with its text                              |
| --------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `neutral` | `color.text.primary` | `color.surface.inset`        | `color.text.primary`       | `color.surface.inverse`, with `color.text.inverse`     |
| `brand`   | `color.text.brand`   | `color.surface.brand-subtle` | none                       | `color.surface.brand`, with `color.text.on-color.dark` |
| `success` | `color.text.success` | `color.surface.success`      | `color.status.success`     | none                                                   |
| `warning` | `color.text.warning` | `color.surface.warning`      | `color.status.warning`     | none                                                   |
| `danger`  | `color.text.danger`  | `color.surface.danger`       | `color.status.danger`      | none                                                   |
| `info`    | `color.text.info`    | `color.surface.info`         | `color.status.info`        | none                                                   |

`brand` is the primary colour: a brand button marks the main action, with `color.surface.brand-hover` on hover and a `color.border.brand` edge, and `color.text.brand` labels its outline. It is never a link. Each action component (Button, IconButton, a Toolbar's buttons) offers `brand` beside `neutral`; the default stays `neutral`, so a screen has one brand action at most. The status intents have no solid fill, because no text colour is measured on `color.status.*`.

## State and events

MUI's names, with Base UI's details passed through as the last argument.

- **Value:** `value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange(event, value, details)`. `details` is Base UI's event details for the change, unchanged: its `reason`, `cancel()` and the rest. `event` is `details.event`.
- **Native text:** a component whose value lives in a native `<input>` or `<textarea>` renders that element as its root and passes React's own `onChange(event)`, `value` and `defaultValue`. React Hook Form's `register()` and Formik's `handleChange` then work unchanged.
- **Open:** `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen(event, details)` and `onClose(event, reason, details)`, where `reason` is `details.reason`.
- **Adapt once:** each component turns Base UI's `onValueChange(value, details)` and `onOpenChange(open, details)` into these, inside itself, and exposes neither.
- **Forms:** a composite control (Select, Checkbox, Radio group, Switch, Slider, Combobox) takes `name` and gives it to Base UI's root, so Base UI's hidden input reaches a native `<form>` and `FormData`. Form libraries connect through their controller: `Controller` in React Hook Form, `useField` in Formik.

## Root

- `ref` and the rest props reach the root element. React 19 passes `ref` as a prop, so the props type declares it.
- `{...rest}` comes before the component's own attributes, so the component's own win: `<BaseButton {...rest} ref={ref} data-variant={variant} className={…}>`.
- `className` is merged, not replaced: `pn-<Name>` first, then the caller's.
- Every prop the props type declares is taken out of `rest` before the spread, so a prop that is invalid on the element never reaches the DOM.

The contract story, `storybook/contract/Contract.stories.tsx`, renders every registered component and pattern past designing with a `ref` and a `data-testid`, and fails unless both land on one element. It renders each with the args of its `Default` story (or its first story) over its meta's, so those args must render it alone, and a new component needs no edit to the contract story.

## Customising

- **`render`** is Base UI's: it swaps the root element and keeps the behaviour, class and data attributes. `<Button render={<a href="/map" />}>`.
- **`slotProps`** is keyed by the Base UI part, its name in camelCase: `Select.Positioner` is `positioner`, `Select.Popup` is `popup`. Each value is that part's props, merged with Base UI's `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`), the component's own props last. The root has no key; it takes the component's own props.
- A caller restyles through `className`, on the root or in `slotProps`, with the tokens.

## Change

Deprecate, never remove. An old prop or value keeps working: the component maps it to its replacement, and its JSDoc says `@deprecated Use <replacement> instead.`

`packages/perron/api.json` is the props API of every `stable` or `deprecated` component: each member its props type declares, whether it is optional, its type, and what the type extends. `npm run api` writes it from the code, and `npm run check` fails while it is stale.

Against `api.json` at the last release tag, `@mylder/perron@<version>`, the API only grows: a new optional prop, a prop made optional, a wider union, a new base. A prop removed, narrowed or made required, a new required prop, a base dropped or a component removed is a break.

### Breaking changes

A deliberate break is a row of this table, which the check reads: the component, the prop (`extends` for a base the props type dropped, `*` for the whole component) and the reason. Take the row out once the release that ships the break is out.

| Component | Prop | Reason |
| --------- | ---- | ------ |

## Styling

- **Classes:** `pn-<Name>` on the root, `pn-<Name>-<part>` on each inner part, with the part named as in `slotProps`: `pn-Button-icon`, `pn-Select-popup`.
- **Data attributes:** the root always carries `data-variant`, `data-color` and `data-size` with the prop's value, defaults included, if the component has the prop. A boolean that changes the look sets a bare attribute named after it: `fullWidth` sets `data-full-width`. Base UI adds its own states: `data-disabled`, `data-pressed`, `data-checked`, `data-highlighted`, `data-open`, `data-popup-open`.
- **Selectors:** one class, then attributes: `.pn-Button[data-variant='outlined'][data-size='small']`.
- **Tokens stay on `:root`.** Popups render in a portal outside the component, so component CSS never redefines a token. The one `--perron-*` property a component sets is `--perron-icon-size`.

## Design states

Hover, focus, pressed, disabled, open and selected are CSS states, read from pseudo-classes and Base UI's attributes. Penpot's `State` property maps to these, never to a prop.

| State       | Selector                                                   |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover       | `:hover`, inside `@media (hover: hover)`                   |
| Highlighted | `[data-highlighted]`, a row under the pointer or the keys  |
| Focus       | `:focus-visible`, with the ring `perron.css` already draws |
| Pressed     | `:active`, `[data-pressed]`                                |
| Disabled    | `[data-disabled]`, `:disabled`                             |
| Open        | `[data-popup-open]` on a trigger, `[data-open]` on a popup |
| Selected    | `[data-selected]`, `[data-checked]`                        |
| Invalid     | `[data-invalid]`                                           |

A component that draws its own focus ring uses `focus.width`, `focus.offset` and `color.border.focus`, as [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md#focus-ring) says.

## CSS

Tokens only.

- Every colour, length, duration, shadow and font is `var(--perron-…)` or a `calc()` over them. The literals allowed are `0`, percentages, unitless numbers and keywords such as `auto`, `none`, `inherit`, `transparent` and `currentColor`.
- `var()` has no fallback: `var(--perron-space-200)`.
- Every `--perron-*` name read is a token in `packages/perron/tokens/`. A typography role brings its `-tracking` twin: `font: var(--perron-typography-label)` with `letter-spacing: var(--perron-typography-label-tracking)`.
- Each layer reads the tokens of its row in [Token families](#token-families).
- **Icons** are sized by setting `--perron-icon-size` to an `icon.size.*` token on the element that holds them. See [Icons](../foundations/icons.md#sizes).
- **Motion** takes `duration.*` and `easing.*`. A state with no fitting duration changes at once; a new one goes through the `design-tokens` skill. A loop (`infinite`) stops inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, in a rule with the loop's own selector that sets its `animation`. See [Motion](../foundations/motion.md).
- **Stacking:** everything that renders in a portal (popups, tooltips, dialogs) takes `z-index.dialog`, so the one opened last paints on top. The other `z-index.*` tokens order the map screen's panels, for patterns.
- **Themes:** the semantic tokens carry both, so component CSS has no `[data-theme]` selector and no `prefers-color-scheme` query.
- **Media queries:** the three in [Media queries](#media-queries). A component sizes to its container.
- Disabled is a colour, `color.text.tertiary`, never an opacity.

### Token families

The tokens each layer's CSS reads. `palette.*` stays behind the semantic tokens.

| Layer                     | Reads                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Component and shared part | `color.text.*`, `color.surface.*`, `color.border.*`, `color.status.*`, `color.scrim`, `typography.*`, `font.*`, `space.*`, `size.*`, `radius.*`, `border.width.*`, `focus.*`, `icon.size.*`, `shadow.*`, `effect.*`, `duration.*`, `easing.*`, `z-index.dialog`, and for Mylder's vocabulary (line badges, delays, Prik) `color.transit.*`, `color.data-state.*` and `prik.*` |
| Pattern                   | A component's, and `color.map.*`, `map.*`, `color.chart.*`, `opacity.*` and every `z-index.*`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

### Media queries

| Query                              | For                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `(hover: hover)`                   | Hover, as [Design states](#design-states) says                                                                                               |
| `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` | Stopping a loop                                                                                                                              |
| `(forced-colors: active)`          | Forced colours, the one place CSS system colours are allowed: `Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `Highlight`, `HighlightText`, `ButtonText`, `GrayText` |

### Families

Members of a family share one treatment, in Penpot and in CSS. A new member joins its family's row; it never gets a surface of its own.

| Family   | Members                                                  | Fill                                                                                                          | Border                                                                           | Radius                                                      | Hover                                                                             | Selected                                          |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Rows     | Options, menu items, list rows, table rows               | None                                                                                                          | None. Where the design divides rows: `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle` | `radius.md` inside a popup; none in a table                 | `color.surface.hover`, on hover and on `[data-highlighted]`                       | `color.surface.selected`, with the `SelectedMark` |
| Fields   | Text inputs, select and combobox triggers, number fields | `color.surface.raised`                                                                                        | `border.width.025` in `color.border.control`; `color.status.danger` when invalid | `radius.md`                                                 | `color.surface.hover` laid over the fill, as a `linear-gradient` background-image | None: an open trigger keeps its rest look         |
| Popups   | Menus, select and combobox lists, popovers               | `color.surface.overlay`, `backdrop-filter` of `effect.glass-blur` and `effect.glass-saturate`, `shadow.panel` | `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`                                      | `radius.lg`, padded `space.100`, so rows' `radius.md` nests | None                                                                              | None                                              |
| Panels   | Dialogs, drawers                                         | As popups. A modal one sits over `color.scrim`                                                                | `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`                                      | `radius.xl`                                                 | None                                                                              | None                                              |
| Tooltips | Tooltips                                                 | `color.surface.inverse`, text `color.text.inverse`, no shadow                                                 | None                                                                             | `radius.md`                                                 | None                                                                              | None                                              |

- Text: rows and buttons in `typography.label`, a row's second line in `typography.caption` with `color.text.secondary`, fields in `typography.body`, tooltips in `typography.label-sm`. A placeholder and anything disabled is `color.text.tertiary`.
- Height: a field is `size.input` tall. A row is at least `size.target-min`.

## Shared parts

Each of these is drawn once, in its own folder, `packages/perron/src/parts/<Part>/` (`<Part>.tsx` and `<Part>.css`). A component composes the part; it never draws its own. Parts are internal: not registered, not exported. A new shared part joins this table first.

| Part                | Draws                                       | Composed in                                                                 | Only its folder holds                                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `VisuallyHidden`    | Text for screen readers only                | Any component with a word the eye gets from an icon or a shape              | `pn-VisuallyHidden`, and `clip-path: inset(50%)` or `clip:` |
| `CheckboxIndicator` | A checkbox's box, with its tick or dash     | `Checkbox.Indicator`, `Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator`                          | `pn-CheckboxIndicator`, and the tick icon                   |
| `SelectedMark`      | The tick beside a chosen option             | `Select.ItemIndicator`, `Combobox.ItemIndicator`, `Menu.RadioItemIndicator` | `pn-SelectedMark`, and the tick icon                        |
| `CloseButton`       | The icon button that closes what it sits in | `Dialog.Close`, `Popover.Close`, `Drawer.Close`, `Toast.Close`              | `pn-CloseButton`, and the `close` icon                      |

- `CloseButton`'s label is the owned string for "Close", overridden by the component's `closeLabel`.
- The tick is not in `packages/perron/icons/` yet. The first part that needs it adds it, following [Icons](../foundations/icons.md).

## What axe won't catch

Every spec copies this checklist, and the build's self-gate and the reviewer tick it against the accessibility tree of every story.

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told: an `aria-hidden` mark has a text equivalent, for every shape the prop accepts.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name, from the component's own heading through `aria-labelledby` where it has one.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden, by its `*Label` prop.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: a `ReactNode` prop shows a string, an element and a list alike.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`.
- [ ] Native semantics first: `<button>`, `<a href>`, `<input>` and Base UI's roles, with ARIA only for what no element says.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order, and closing anything returns it to where it came from.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion.

The rest of the WCAG 2.2 AA target is on [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md).

## Words

- Visible content comes from the caller, as `children` or a prop: a button's text, a dialog's title.
- A string the component owns, such as a pagination button's "Previous page" or a dialog's "Close", comes from the locale dictionaries in `packages/perron/src/locale/` (`en.ts`, `da.ts`, `sv.ts`, `nb.ts`), in the locale `PerronProvider` sets. A new one is a key in `en.ts` and in each of the others.
- Each owned string has a `<key>Label` prop that overrides it on one instance: `close` is `closeLabel`. The component reads its strings with the overrides laid over them: `const strings = useOwnedStrings({ close: closeLabel })`, from `packages/perron/src/PerronProvider.tsx`.
- Owned strings follow [content design](../content-design.md): sentence case, the fixed data-state words, no exclamation marks. The spec gives the English; agents write the Danish, Swedish and Norwegian.
- `expectOwnedStrings(markup, locale, callerStrings)`, from `packages/perron/src/testing/owned-strings.ts`, fails a render that shows or announces a word neither the locale's dictionary nor the caller gave. The contract story runs it over every component (see [Stories](#stories)); a component with more words in another state, such as an open dialog's close label, calls it in its own test on that render: `expectOwnedStrings(renderToStaticMarkup(<PerronProvider locale="da">…</PerronProvider>), 'da', ['Departures'])`.

## Stories

- The default export is `satisfies Meta<typeof <Name>>`, with `component` set and `title: 'Components/<Name>'`.
- One story per variant and state the Penpot design shows, named as Penpot names it, so the visual check pairs each story with its export.
- A `play` test for every behaviour the component promises (dismissal, focus, keyboard), ending in the resting state: popups closed and focus back where it started.
- Stories run in Chromium with axe in `error` mode (`npm run test:stories`, part of `npm run check`), so an axe violation fails CI. The contract story's `Keyboard` story is the `play` pattern to copy: Tab to the element, expect focus, Shift+Tab back.
- The contract story's `OwnedStrings` story renders every component and pattern with the args its `Root` story takes (see [Root](#root)), in `en`, `da`, `sv` and `nb`, and runs `expectOwnedStrings` on each render, with the strings in those args as the caller's words. So those args hold every word the caller gives.

## Patterns

A pattern is a piece of a Mylder screen, such as a departure row. It follows this contract, with three differences:

- Its files are in `packages/perron/src/patterns/<Name>/`, in the same four shapes, its stories are titled `Patterns/<Name>`, and its spec is `docs/patterns/<name>.md`.
- Its code imports only Perron's components and parts, `PerronProvider`, React and the files of its own folder, never `@base-ui/react`. A type-only import from another package is fine, and its stories and tests are not its code.
- It takes Mylder's domain props, such as a departure or a line, and its CSS reads the pattern row of [Token families](#token-families).

It is exported from `@mylder/perron/patterns`.

## Checks

Each rule is one script, `scripts/checks/<rule>.ts`. `npm run gates` runs them all, as part of `npm run check`, and `npm run gates -- <rule>` runs one. A deliberate exception is written in place, on the line it excuses or the line above it, with one rule and a reason:

```css
/* perron-allow(component-css): the map canvas reads this length in script */
```

In Markdown it is an HTML comment holding `perron-allow(paths): reason`, at the end of the line it excuses: prettier sets a comment on its own line apart from the text below it. A rule whose breach has no line, `docs` and `api-compatibility`, takes no allowance, and nor does `penpot`, whose files are JSON. Every run of the gates also fails an allowance that names no rule or gives no reason, wherever it is.

| Rule                | Fails on                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `component-css`     | A [CSS](#css) rule broken: a raw value, a `var()` fallback, a `--perron-*` name no token defines, a token outside its layer's [families](#token-families), a query outside [Media queries](#media-queries), a loop that never stops                                                                 |
| `props`             | A `<Name>Props`, read with the TypeScript compiler, outside the [Props](#props) table's types, with a [name from other libraries](#names-from-other-libraries), an `is`, `has` or `should` boolean, or a member without JSDoc                                                                       |
| `patterns`          | A [pattern](#patterns) importing anything but Perron components and parts                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `shared-parts`      | A [shared part](#shared-parts)'s class, icon or declarations outside its folder                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `docs`              | A registered entry without its spec from `building` on, its `<Name>.mdx` from `stable` on (see [Files](#files)), code from which the docs page's docgen reads no props, a member without a spec Props row or a row without a member, or a prop whose default it reads otherwise than the spec gives |
| `api-compatibility` | A `stable` or `deprecated` entry's props API shrinking against the last release tag (see [Change](#change))                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `paths`             | A path a doc or skill names, in a link or a code span, that does not exist                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `penpot`            | A design read back with an unknown token, an unbound value, or an unmapped variant or layer                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

title: Spec template
markdown:
# Spec template

The page every component's spec starts from. The `component-brief` skill copies it to `docs/components/<name>.md` and fills it from the read-back (`penpot/<name>.json`), the code map (`penpot/<name>.code-map.json`) and `get_reference` for each Base UI part, by the rules of the [contract](../components/README.md).

How to fill it:

- Replace this heading with the component's name, `# Button`, and this paragraph and list with one sentence on what the component is for.
- Fill every `<…>` placeholder, and replace the example rows with the component's own.
- Write a question the sources can't answer in place, as `[PENDING] <the question>`, and put it to the maintainer. The spec is done when every section is filled and no `[PENDING]` is left.
- Link only a page the docs site serves: the foundations, the guidelines, the contract and the other specs. Write any other repo path, such as an ADR (`docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), `penpot/README.md` or the read-back, as a code span, as the contract does; `scripts/lib/site.test.ts` fails on a link the site can't follow.
- Keep every section, in this order. A section that doesn't apply says why in one line: "No owned strings: every word comes from the caller."

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/<Name>`. Family: `<Rows | Fields | Popups | Panels | Tooltips | none>`. Shared parts: `<VisuallyHidden, CheckboxIndicator, SelectedMark, CloseButton, or none>`.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                      | Base UI part         | Class              | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------ | --------------- |
| `root`              | `<what the root is>`            | `<Component>.Root`   | `pn-<Name>`        | none            |
| `<part>`            | `<what this part is and holds>` | `<Component>.<Part>` | `pn-<Name>-<part>` | `<part>`        |

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/<component>`, at the version pinned in `package.json`.

| Base UI part         | Renders     | Perron sets                                 | Passed through               |
| -------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `<Component>.Root`   | `<element>` | `<props the component sets, and from what>` | `<props the caller reaches>` |
| `<Component>.<Part>` | `<element>` | `<…>`                                       | `slotProps.<part>`           |

Base UI already does: `<behaviour Base UI handles, such as typeahead or focus return>`.

## Props

In MUI's layout, one row per prop the docs page shows, slots last: each prop the component declares, its description becoming the JSDoc, and each it inherits from Base UI, such as `render`, which reads `inherited` under Base UI prop and gives Base UI's type, default and description while the code inherits it as it is (the contract's [Props](../components/README.md#props)).

| Name               | Type                              | Default      | Base UI prop         | Description                  |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `variant`          | `'<value>' \| '<value>'`          | `'<value>'`  | none                 | `<what each value is for>`   |
| `size`             | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'`  | `'medium'`   | none                 | `<…>`                        |
